topics.title: Privacy and data
topics.summary: Do not enter protected data without the required prior IDG or Research Ethics approval. A Warwick-account Copilot recommendation is not that approval.

claims.text: Warwick's AI Information Compliance Policy says certain data, including personal or confidential material, University intellectual property, and some copyrighted or third-party data, must not be put into AI software without prior approval.

evidence.quote: Certain types of data must never be put into any AI software, without prior approval from IDG or the Research Ethics Committee. These include: Passwords and usernames. Personally identifiable information (PII) or other sensitive or confidential material. Any data related to University Intellectual Property.
evidence.title: IMP 02: AI Information Compliance Policy

claims.text: Warwick's student-facing guidance tells students not to enter personal or confidential data into AI tools unless they understand what will happen to the data, and recommends Copilot chat with a Warwick account for that kind of data.

evidence.quote: Do not input any personal or confidential data into any AI tools, unless you fully understand what will happen to that data. The university recommends using Co-Pilot chat for this kind of data - when logged in with your Warwick account.

topics.title: Research and publication
topics.summary: Research guidance requires researchers to consider AI-related risks and retain responsibility, including for misconduct arising inadvertently through a tool.
topics.scope: Assessment briefs and course handbooks control student use; research, procurement and data approvals have their own scope. Research guidance requires researchers to consider AI-related risks and retain responsibility, including for misconduct arising inadvertently through a tool.

claims.text: Warwick's AI in research guidance says its principles apply to all researchers and researchers must consider AI-related research risks including integrity, information security, and accountability risks.

evidence.quote: The principles set out in this guidance apply to all researchers as previously defined. Researchers must consider all risks that may be relevant to their research that arise from AI.
evidence.title: AI in Research
evidence.location: Who is expected to use this guidance / Risk Considerations

claims.text: Warwick's AI in research guidance says researchers are responsible for misconduct-type practices involving AI, including improper handling of information or use of another person's ideas, even if such practices occur inadvertently through an AI tool.

evidence.quote: Misconduct in research includes: the fabrication or falsification of research data; improper handling of information on individuals collected during research; or the use of another person's ideas, work or research data without appropriate acknowledgement. Researchers are responsible for any such practices, even if they occur inadvertently through the use of an AI tool.
evidence.title: AI in Research
evidence.location: Breach of Responsibilities and Expected Standards

topics.evidenceScope: Assessment briefs and course handbooks control student use; research, procurement and data approvals have their own scope. Research guidance requires researchers to consider AI-related risks and retain responsibility, including for misconduct arising inadvertently through a tool.
